candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Determine a common denominator and rewrite fraction parts as equivalent fractions before subtraction when denominators differ.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S01, B.S01, and C.S01 have effectively identical names, definitions, inclusions, and exclusions centered on creating like denominators before subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a whole number, fraction-only quantity, or nonstandard mixed number into a compatible form for subtraction, such as adding a 0-fraction part or converting an improper mixed-number fraction part to standard mixed form.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S02, B.S02, and C.S02 all describe preparatory rewriting of operands into subtraction-ready form; C's definition is slightly broadest and cleanly covers the shared concept.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract fractions with like denominators and/or subtract whole-number and fractional parts once the operands are in compatible form.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts use the same name and nearly identical definitions for the core subtraction step after setup is complete.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Regroup one whole as denominator-over-denominator and add it to the fractional part when the fractional subtraction would otherwise be negative.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S04, B.S04, and C.S04 all represent the same regrouping/borrowing operation in mixed-number or whole-minus-fraction subtraction; only wording differs slightly.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the resulting fraction to lowest terms or simplify a zero-fraction result to a whole number or integer.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: The three S05 skills are direct matches covering reduction to lowest terms and simplification of zero-fraction outcomes.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Combine the computed whole-number and fractional parts and express the result in an acceptable final form such as a mixed number, fraction, or integer.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S06, B.S06, and C.S06 all describe recombining computed parts into the final presented answer; C uses 'form' while A and B use 'answer,' but the concept is the same.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks are highly consistent and align one-to-one across all six skills. Each expert identified the same six cognitive concepts: denominator matching, operand normalization, subtraction of aligned parts, borrowing/regrouping, simplification, and final recomposition. No one-to-many mappings or orphan skills were needed; every skill_id from A, B, and C maps exactly once to a single shared concept.
